blocking_findings.title: An exception after report construction can still publish a report for a failed attempt
evidence: score_b0_blind.py:1025-1061 assigns a non-null report before the successful receipt update has completed.
score_b0_blind.py:1082-1096 catches TechnicalInvalid and every BaseException but neither exception branch unconditionally clears report nor resets technically_valid to false.

A KeyboardInterrupt, MemoryError, or other BaseException delivered after report assignment, including around receipt.update at lines 1062-1081, therefore reaches the terminal stage with report still non-null. If interruption occurs after receipt.update returns, technically_valid may also remain true while status is rewritten as a failure.

score_b0_blind.py:1115-1128 decides whether to write report.json solely from report is not None and returns solely from technically_valid. It can therefore publish a failure report, or a contradictory failure-status/technically-valid receipt, through the otherwise atomic staging path.
B0_SCORING_CONTRACT.json:193-200 requires a technical failure to publish only a terminal receipt and never a report.
blocking_findings.impact: A narrow but real asynchronous-exception path violates the blind first-valid-attempt policy: a canonical failed attempt can expose metric output, and in one interleaving can return success from a receipt whose status says failure.
blocking_findings.minimum_strict_fix: In both exception handlers, unconditionally assign report = None and receipt['technically_valid'] = False before recording the failure. Permit report staging only when report is non-null, receipt.status is exactly PASS_B0_MACHINE_SCORE_SINGLE_ROW_COHORT_INCOMPLETE, and technically_valid is exactly true. On every other terminal state, require that no staged report exists. Before atomic publication, validate the same success/report iff invariant from the staged terminal receipt. Do not change any metric, ROI, pair, threshold, tensor, camera, or claim logic.
